_comment: LG AC IR codebook, captured 2026-09-06 (Phase 3). Not a lookup table of buttons: LG encodes the FULL target state in every frame, so the brain constructs frames from these field encodings. See mac/lg_ir.py for the encoder and its self-test against the verified samples below.

frame.layout: n1 n2 n3 n4 n5 n6 n7  (7 nibbles, MSB first)
frame.n3: 0x0 for state frames; 0xC marks the special power-off command
frame.checksum: sum of the six preceding nibbles, masked with 0xF

mode._encoding: 0x8 + mode_index, matching the standard LG AC mode order
mode._heat_note: Not present in this remote's mode cycle (cool -> auto -> dry -> fan -> cool). The LG order implies heat would be 0xC, but that is UNVERIFIED and must not be fired until captured from a remote that offers it. Treat heat as unsupported.

fan._comment: The remote exposes 5 speeds + auto. We expose the canonical LG subset (speeds 1/3/5 + auto); the half-steps are captured but deliberately not exposed by the tool schema.

commands._power_on_note: There is no separate power-on frame: any state frame turns the unit on with that state, which is what makes the stateless model work. The REMOTE (not the AC) remembers the last state and resends it as a full frame when powered on — which is why no distinct 'on' code exists. Sina deliberately cannot reproduce 'last state', since tracking it is exactly the synthetic state mirror invariant 2 forbids; set_power:on therefore fires the default_preset from mac/config.json, which is config rather than state. STILL UNVERIFIED: 0x8800606 was observed from the power button and does not parse as a state frame (its mode nibble is 0x0, outside the valid 0x8-0xB range), so it is some other command class. Confirm with the transmitter before relying on any of this.
commands._jet_note: LG calls this 'Po' on the display. Verified in isolation: one press emits exactly this one frame. The remote exits jet by sending a normal STATE frame (observed: 0x880834F = cool/18C/high), NOT by resending this code — so this reads as 'enter jet', not 'toggle jet', and stays stateless. Exiting jet therefore needs no dedicated code: any state frame does it, which set_preset already fires. TO VERIFY IN PHASE 4: send this frame while the unit is already in jet and confirm it does not exit — if it does, this is a toggle after all and must be exposed as such.
commands._light_note: Toggles the unit's display light. Confirmed a BLIND TOGGLE: identical frame every press, and the light went off then back on. There is no separate on/off code and no way to read current state, so the resulting state is genuinely unknowable — expose it as toggle_light, never as set_light(on=bool), per invariant 3. This is the one command where 'fire and cannot verify' is inherent rather than a gap in the capture.

_unidentified.0x88C0F50: seen during the jet/sleep batch; shares the 0xC command marker with power_off

verified_samples._comment: Every entry below was captured from the physical remote and passes the LG checksum. mac/lg_ir.py regenerates each one as its self-test.

mode_sweep._comment: The remote keeps separate temp/fan memory per mode, hence the varying temp and fan here.
